sq.q: Write a Java method that takes an array of integers as input and returns a new array with each element doubled.
answer: public class ArrayUtils { public static int[] doubleArray(int[] input) { int[] result = new int[input.length]; for (int i = 0; i < input.length; i++) { result[i] = input[i] * 2; } return result; } } This method demonstrates array manipulation and returning arrays from methods.

sq.q: Differentiate between a one-dimensional and a two-dimensional array in Java with examples.
answer: A one-dimensional array is a linear collection of elements, e.g., int[] numbers = {1, 2, 3}; A two-dimensional array is like a table with rows and columns, e.g., int[][] matrix = { {1, 2}, {3, 4} }; Access in 1D: numbers[1] = 2 Access in 2D: matrix[1][0] = 3

lq.q: You are building a student result system. Each student has marks in 3 subjects. You are given an array of student objects, and each object contains the student name and marks. Write a Java program that does the following: Uses an array of Student objects Passes the array to a method that calculates and prints each student�s average mark
answer: Java Code: class Student { String name; int[] marks; Student(String name, int[] marks) { this.name = name; this.marks = marks; } } public class StudentResults { public static void calculateAverages(Student[] students) { for (Student s : students) { int total = 0; for (int mark : s.marks) { total += mark; } double avg = (double) total / s.marks.length; System.out.println("Student: " + s.name + " | Average: " + avg); } } public static void main(String[] args) { Student[] studentArray = { new Student("Alice", new int[]{85, 90, 88}), new Student("Bob", new int[]{70, 65, 75}) }; calculateAverages(studentArray); } } Explanation: An array of objects (Student[]) stores multiple student records. The method calculateAverages() accepts the array and processes each object. This modular approach supports code reuse, clarity, and object-oriented handling of structured data.
